headlines.title: China’s factory-gate prices growth slows to 3.5% in July amid lower fuel prices
headlines.summary:
China’s factory-gate prices growth slowed in July, as lower domestic fuel prices eased cost pressures triggered by the US-Israel war on Iran, while high temperatures dragged manufacturing.
The producer price index (PPI) rose by 3.5 per cent year on year last month, compared with 4.1 per cent in June, according to data released by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) on Sunday.

headlines.summary_en: The Ministry of Finance will issue RMB 6 billion in treasury bonds in Macau on August 20. headlines.title_en: A-share close: Shanghai index rises 0.67% for 5 consecutive gains, with pharmaceutical and consumer stocks strengthening collectively
headlines.summary_en: The market diverged throughout the day, with the three major indices mixed. Consumer stocks such as food strengthened, with Huangshi Group, Xiangpiaopiao, and Yiming Food hitting the daily limit. Pharma stocks extended gains, with Baihua Pharma hitting a 5-day consecutive limit, and multiple stocks including Yatai Pharma and Hayao Co. hitting the daily limit. Gold stocks fluctuated higher, with Zhaojin Gold, CHJ, and Mankaron hitting the daily limit. The military industry sector was active, with Hongdu Aviation, Hunan Tianyan, and Great Wall Military hitting the daily limit. On the downside, computing hardware stocks such as PCB and CPO declined, with Taijin New Energy falling over 8%. More stocks rose than fell, with over 4,000 stocks in the Shanghai, Shenzhen, and Beijing markets in the red, and turnover near RMB 2.54 trillion today. At the close, the Shanghai Composite Index rose 0.67%, the Shenzhen Component Index rose 0.04%, and the ChiNext Index fell 0.73%.

headlines.title_en: Midday close on August 10: ChiNext index falls over 2% in half-day trading, while pharmaceutical and consumer stocks rise against the trend
headlines.summary_en: 1. The market diverged clearly in the morning, with the Shanghai Composite Index trading in the red and the ChiNext Index falling over 2%. Pharma stocks extended gains, with Baihua Pharma hitting a 5-day consecutive limit, and multiple stocks including Yatai Pharma, Ha Sanlian, and Hisun Pharma hitting the daily limit. Consumer stocks such as food bucked the trend higher, with Huangshi Group, Xiangpiaopiao, and Yiming Food hitting the daily limit. The military industry sector moved up sharply, with Hunan Tianyan and Great Wall Military hitting the daily limit. On the downside, computing hardware stocks such as PCB and CPO declined, with Accelink Technologies nearing the daily limit, and Changyingtong and Taijin New Energy falling over 10%. More stocks rose than fell, with over 3,400 stocks in the Shanghai, Shenzhen, and Beijing markets in the red, and morning turnover of RMB 1.75 trillion. At midday close, the Shanghai Composite Index rose 0.2%, the Shenzhen Component Index fell 1.13%, and the ChiNext fell 2.18%. 2. headlines.title_en: ETF close | ChiNext index falls 0.73%, agriculture and aquaculture sectors strengthen, with aquaculture ETF and agriculture-aquaculture-fishery ETF rising 3%
headlines.summary_en: The Shanghai Composite Index closed up 0.67%, while the ChiNext Index fell 0.73%. Major consumer sectors strengthened, with baijiu and food leading gains; pharma and biotech stocks were active, with innovative drugs surging; coal, infrastructure, military industry, and gold sectors were among the top gainers. The computing hardware supply chain adjusted, with server, CPO, and memory indices leading declines. Over 4,000 stocks rose in the market. Private enterprise, agricultural farming, semiconductor equipment, biotech, and gold sectors strengthened, with related ETFs closing broadly higher, gaining between 2.89% and 9.41%: Private enterprise sector: Qiantu Kaiyuan Private Enterprise 300 ETF rose 9.41%, leading gains in the private enterprise theme. Agricultural farming sector: Guotai Farming ETF rose 3.58%; HuaTai柏瑞 Farming ETF rose 3.36%; Huabao Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Fishery ETF rose 3.16%; Yifangda Agriculture ETF rose 2.96%, with the agricultural farming track continuing.
